units.title: Colonialism and Independence Movements in Latin America

lessons.title: Colonialism and Independence Movements in Latin America

cards.title: Colonialism and Independence Movements in Latin America
body: After the treaty of Tordesilas both Portugal and Spain tried to consolidate their grasp in Latin America especially in the 16th c Portugal controlled Brazil but Spain created a very vast empire in here.

cards.title: Creation of a new Society
body: In 1501 Spain allowed the intermarriage of natives and Spaniards this created different people like the MESTIZOES (European and Latin American offspring), MULATTOSE, and other African European offspring's.
Economic benefits for the Europeans came from; Mining (gold and silver), creation of immense state by the Europeans in Farming, and trade.
Christianizing the natives was giving to Catholic Church. Besides the Catholic Church built cathedrals, orphanages, schools and hospitals.
The colonialism created new social structure with peninsular (European viceroys) at the top and creoles European and native descendants at the middle and mestizos.
The national movement in L.A started by the middle class, especially after the Napoleonic wars the creoles started organizing revolutions.
On January 1, 1804, the western part of Hispaniola, now called Haiti, announced its freedom and became the first independent state in Latin America.
Beginning in 1810, Mexico too, experienced a revolt. The first leader of Mexican independence movement was a priest called Miguel Hidalgo. In 1821, Mexico declared its independence from Spain.
Starting from 1801-1825 all L.A got freedom led by famous nationalist like Simon Bolivar and Jose de san Martin.

cards.title: Post-independence problems
body: Weak gov’t unable to run the new republicans
Economic problems led them to dependency upon the former colonizers
The reign of caudillos began with military force and only work for the land owners.
And later the USA dominance came As a result of
the Spanish-American War (1898), Cuba became a United States
protectorate, and Puerto Rico was annexed to the United States. In

1903, the United States supported a rebellion that enabled Panama to separate itself from Colombia and establish a new state. In return, the United States was given a narrow piece of land 16 km wide running from coast to coast in Panama
At last in 1870 the prosperity for L.A starts and the growth middleclass came After 1900, Latin Americans also
increased their own industrialization, especially by building textile,
